title: Projective direct-image constructibility
statement:
Every projective morphism
between schemes of finite type over $k$ satisfies
$\mathcal C(f)$ of [def-finrepair-property-c].

proof.text: Fix the finite coefficient ring $\Lambda$ occurring in [def-finrepair-property-c]. For an arbitrary finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, [thm-fin-projective-line-constructible] says that $R^q\pi_*F$ is constructible for every constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $F$ on $\mathbf P^1_T$ and every $q\geq0$, where $\pi:\mathbf P^1_T\to T$. The coefficient ring and invertible annihilating integer are precisely the fixed ones in the definition of $\mathcal C$. Thus, by [def-finrepair-property-c], $\mathcal C(\mathbf P^1_T\to T)$ holds. Since $T$ was arbitrary, this supplies the universally quantified hypothesis of the reduction lemma.

Apply [lem-finrepair-projective-from-line] to the assertion for every finite-type base obtained in step 1. Its conclusion gives $\mathcal C(f)$ for every projective morphism $f:X\to S$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, exactly as required. The projective convention [def-pc-projective-morphism] is the projective-space-embedding convention used in the reduction; no extension to arbitrary proper morphisms, change of coefficient category, or uniform vanishing assertion is involved.
